sentences.chinese: 時或傳襄創重不濟，溫軍所得士女莫不北望揮涕。
sentences.literal: At times rumor spread that Xiang's wounds were grave and he would not recover; among the men and women taken by Wen's army there was none who did not look north and wipe tears.
sentences.idiomatic: From time to time word ran that Yao Xiang's wounds were mortal and he would not survive; every soldier's wife and captive commoner in Huan Wen's host gazed northward and wept.

sentences.chinese: 其得物情如此。
sentences.literal: Thus did he win the people's hearts.
sentences.idiomatic: Such was the devotion he commanded among the people.

sentences.chinese: 先是，弘農楊亮歸襄，襄待以客禮。
sentences.literal: Earlier, Yang Liang of Hongnong had come over to Xiang, and Xiang treated him with guest courtesy.
sentences.idiomatic: Earlier, Yang Liang of Hongnong had defected to Yao Xiang, who received him with the rites due an honored guest.

sentences.chinese: 後奔桓溫，溫問襄於亮，亮曰：「神明器宇，孫策之儔，而雄武過之。
sentences.literal: Later he fled to Huan Wen; Wen asked Liang about Xiang, and Liang said: "In divine bearing and imposing presence he is a match for Sun Ce, yet in heroic martial prowess he surpasses him.
sentences.idiomatic: He later fled to Huan Wen, who asked Yang Liang what manner of man Yao Xiang was. Liang replied, "He has the aura of a born leader—Sun Ce's peer, and even more formidable in arms."

sentences.chinese: 」其見重如是。
sentences.literal: Thus was he esteemed.
sentences.idiomatic: Such was the esteem he inspired.

sentences.chinese: 萇字景茂，弋仲第二十四子也。
sentences.literal: Chang, courtesy name Jingmao, was Yizhong's twenty-fourth son.
sentences.idiomatic: Yao Chang, whose courtesy name was Jingmao, was the twenty-fourth son of Yao Yizhong.

sentences.chinese: 少聰哲，多權略，廓落任率，不修行業，諸兄皆奇之。
sentences.literal: From youth he was clever and wise, full of stratagems, broad-minded and unrestrained, and did not cultivate conduct; his elder brothers all marveled at him.
sentences.idiomatic: Even as a boy he was sharp and resourceful, fond of schemes yet openhanded and free in his ways, careless of formal self-cultivation; each of his older brothers regarded him as extraordinary.

sentences.chinese: 隨襄征伐，每參大謀。
sentences.literal: He followed Xiang on campaigns and always took part in great plans.
sentences.idiomatic: He rode with Yao Xiang on every campaign and was consulted on the weightiest decisions.

sentences.chinese: 襄之寇洛陽也，夢萇服袞衣，升御坐，諸酋長皆侍立，旦謂將佐曰：「吾夢如此，此兒志度不恆，或能大起吾族。
sentences.literal: When Xiang raided Luoyang, he dreamed that Chang wore ceremonial robes, ascended the imperial seat, and all the chieftains stood attendance; at dawn he told his officers: "My dream was thus—this boy's aims and bearing are not ordinary; perhaps he can greatly raise our clan.
sentences.idiomatic: While Yao Xiang was striking toward Luoyang he dreamed that Yao Chang stood robed as an emperor on the throne while tribal chiefs waited on him in ranks. At daybreak he told his staff, "I have seen such a dream. The lad's ambition is no common thing; he may yet exalt our whole line."

sentences.chinese: 」襄之敗于麻田也，馬中流矢死，萇下馬以授襄，襄曰：「汝何以自免？
sentences.literal: " When Xiang was defeated at Madian, his horse was struck by a flying arrow and died; Chang dismounted and gave his mount to Xiang. Xiang said: "How will you save yourself?
sentences.idiomatic: After the rout at Madian, Yao Xiang's horse was killed by a stray shaft; Yao Chang sprang down and pressed the reins into his brother's hand. Yao Xiang cried, "And how will you get away?"

sentences.chinese: 」萇曰：「但令兄濟，豎子安敢害萇！
sentences.literal: " Chang said: "Only let elder brother be delivered—how would some wretch dare harm Chang!
sentences.idiomatic: Yao Chang answered, "If you ride clear, no pack of nobodies will touch me."

sentences.chinese: 」會救至，俱免。
sentences.literal: " When rescue arrived, both escaped.
sentences.idiomatic: Relief came in time, and both men survived.

sentences.chinese: 及襄死，萇率諸弟降于苻生。
sentences.literal: When Xiang died, Chang led his younger brothers to surrender to Fu Sheng.
sentences.idiomatic: After Yao Xiang fell, Yao Chang brought their brothers to submit to Fu Sheng.

sentences.chinese: 苻堅以萇為揚武將軍。
sentences.literal: Fu Jian appointed Chang General Who Raises Might.
sentences.idiomatic: Fu Jian named him General Who Raises Might.

sentences.chinese: 曆左衛將軍，隴東、汲郡、河東、武都、武威、巴西、扶風太守，甯、幽、兗三州刺史，復為揚武將軍，步兵校尉，封益都侯。
sentences.literal: He successively served as General of the Left Guard, Administrator of Longdong, Ji, Hedong, Wudu, Wuwei, Baxi, and Fufeng, Inspector of three provinces—Ning, You, and Yan—was again General Who Raises Might and Colonel of Foot Soldiers, and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Yidu.
sentences.idiomatic: He rose through General of the Left Guard, magistracies across Longdong, Ji, Hedong, Wudu, Wuwei, Baxi, and Fufeng, and inspectorships of Ning, You, and Yan, then returned to the rank of General Who Raises Might and Colonel of Foot Soldiers, with a marquisate at Yidu.

sentences.chinese: 為堅將，累有大功。
sentences.literal: As Jian's general, he repeatedly achieved great merit.
sentences.idiomatic: As Fu Jian's commander he won distinction again and again.

sentences.chinese: 初，萇隨楊安伐蜀，嘗晝寢水旁，上有神光煥然，左右咸異之。
sentences.literal: At first, when Chang followed Yang An to campaign against Shu, he once napped by day beside the water; above him a divine light shone brilliantly, and those around him all thought it strange.
sentences.idiomatic: Long before, while serving under Yang An in the conquest of Shu, Yao Chang dozed by a stream at noon; a supernatural radiance played above him, and every man in his escort knew it for an omen.

sentences.chinese: 及苻堅寇晉，以萇為龍驤將軍、督益、梁州諸軍事，謂萇曰：「朕本以龍驤建業，龍驤之號未曾假人，今特以相授，山南之事一以委卿。
sentences.literal: When Fu Jian invaded Jin, he made Chang Dragon-Soaring General and supervisor of military affairs in Yi and Liang, and said to Chang: "I originally founded my enterprise with the title Dragon-Soaring; I have never lent that style to another—now I specially confer it on you; all matters south of the mountains I wholly entrust to you.
sentences.idiomatic: When Fu Jian marched against Jin he invested Yao Chang as Dragon-Soaring General and gave him command of all forces in Yi and Liang. "The Dragon-Soaring banner built my throne," he said. "I have never given that name away; now it is yours alone. South of the Qinling ridges, your word is law."

sentences.chinese: 」堅左將軍竇沖進曰：「王者無戲言，此將不祥之征也，惟陛下察之。
sentences.literal: " Fu Jian's General of the Left Dou Chong advanced and said: "A king has no jesting words—this generalship is an ill omen; I beg Your Majesty to consider it.
sentences.idiomatic: His general Dou Chong stepped forward. "Sovereigns do not speak in sport," he warned. "That commission is a dark portent. I urge you to reconsider."

sentences.chinese: 」堅默然。
sentences.literal: " Jian was silent.
sentences.idiomatic: Fu Jian said nothing.

sentences.chinese: 堅既敗於淮南，歸長安，慕容泓起兵叛堅。
sentences.literal: After Jian was defeated at Huainan and returned to Chang'an, Murong Hong raised troops in rebellion against Jian.
sentences.idiomatic: After Fu Jian's defeat in Huainan, he withdrew to Chang'an; Murong Hong then rose in revolt.

sentences.chinese: 堅遣子叡討之，以萇為司馬。
sentences.literal: Jian sent his son Rui to punish him and made Chang marshal.
sentences.idiomatic: Fu Jian sent his son Fu Rui against the rebels and named Yao Chang his army marshal.

sentences.chinese: 為泓所敗，叡死之。
sentences.literal: He was defeated by Hong, and Rui died in it.
sentences.idiomatic: Murong Hong shattered the expedition, and Fu Rui died on the field.

sentences.chinese: 萇遣龍驤長史趙都詣堅謝罪，堅怒，殺之。
sentences.literal: Chang sent Dragon-Soaring chief clerk Zhao Du to Jian to apologize for his fault; Jian in anger killed him.
sentences.idiomatic: Yao Chang sent his chief clerk Zhao Du to apologize; Fu Jian, furious, had Zhao executed.

sentences.chinese: 萇懼，奔於渭北，遂如馬牧。
sentences.literal: Chang feared and fled to the north of the Wei, then went to the horse pastures.
sentences.idiomatic: Terror-stricken, Yao Chang bolted across the Wei to the northern pastures.

sentences.chinese: 西州豪族尹詳、趙曜、王欽盧、王欽盧、牛雙、狄廣、張乾等率五萬餘家，咸推萇為盟主。
sentences.literal: Powerful western clans Yin Xiang, Zhao Yao, Wang Qinlu, Wang Qinlu, Niu Shuang, Di Guang, Zhang Qian, and others led more than fifty thousand households and all pushed Chang to be covenant lord.
sentences.idiomatic: Western magnates—Yin Xiang, Zhao Yao, Wang Qinlu, Wang Qinlu (named twice in the text), Niu Shuang, Di Guang, Zhang Qian, and their following—mobilized over fifty thousand households and hailed Yao Chang as their league chief.

sentences.chinese: 萇將距之，天水尹緯說萇曰：「今百六之數既臻，秦亡之兆已見，以將軍威靈命世，必能匡濟時艱，故豪傑驅馳，咸同推仰。
sentences.literal: Chang was about to refuse them; Yin Wei of Tianshui persuaded Chang, saying: "Now the cycle of great calamity has arrived, and the omen of Qin's fall is already manifest; by the general's awe-inspiring mandate over the age you are sure to rescue the age from hardship—therefore heroes gallop to you and together lift you up.
sentences.idiomatic: Yao Chang meant to decline, but Yin Wei of Tianshui urged him on: "The great reckoning is upon us and Former Qin is doomed. Your prestige commands the hour; every bold spirit rallies to you because they believe you alone can save the realm."

sentences.chinese: 明公宜降心從議，以副群望，不可坐觀沈溺而不拯救之。
sentences.literal: The enlightened lord ought to humble his mind and follow their counsel, to match the multitude's hopes; you cannot sit watching them sink and drown without rescuing them.
sentences.idiomatic: Humble your pride, accept their mandate, and answer the hope of the world. You must not watch them founder and do nothing.

sentences.chinese: 」萇乃從緯謀，乙太元九年自稱大將軍、大單于、萬年秦王，大赦境內，年號白雀，稱制行事。
sentences.literal: " Chang then followed Wei's plan; in the ninth year of Jin's Taiyuan era he styled himself Grand General, Great Chanyu, and Prince of Wannian of Qin, proclaimed an amnesty within his borders, adopted the era name White Sparrow, and exercised imperial authority in conducting affairs.
sentences.idiomatic: Yao Chang took Yin Wei's counsel. In the ninth year of the Eastern Jin Taiyuan era he declared himself Grand General, Great Chanyu, and Prince of Wannian of Qin, ordered a general amnesty, chose the reign title White Sparrow, and ruled as regent.

sentences.chinese: 以天水尹詳、南安龐演為左右長史，南安姚晃、尹緯為左右司馬，天水狄伯支、焦虔、梁希、龐魏、任謙為從事中郎，姜訓、閻遵為掾屬，王據、焦世、蔣秀、尹延年、牛雙、張乾為參軍，王欽盧、姚方成、王破虜、楊難、尹嵩、裴騎、趙曜、狄廣、黨刪等為帥。
sentences.literal: He appointed Yin Xiang of Tianshui and Pang Yan of Nan'an as left and right senior clerks; Yao Huang of Nan'an and Yin Wei as left and right majors; Di Bozhi, Jiao Qian, Liang Xi, Pang Wei, and Ren Qian of Tianshui as attendant clerks; Jiang Xun and Yan Zun as staff aides; Wang Ju, Jiao Shi, Jiang Xiu, Yin Yannian, Niu Shuang, and Zhang Qian as military advisers; and Wang Qinlu, Yao Fangcheng, Wang Polu, Yang Nan, Yin Song, Pei Qi, Zhao Yao, Di Guang, Dang Shan, and others as commanders.
sentences.idiomatic: He named Yin Xiang of Tianshui and Pang Yan of Nan'an his senior clerks, Yao Huang and Yin Wei his majors, Di Bozhi, Jiao Qian, Liang Xi, Pang Wei, and Ren Qian attendant clerks, Jiang Xun and Yan Zun administrative aides, Wang Ju, Jiao Shi, Jiang Xiu, Yin Yannian, Niu Shuang, and Zhang Qian staff advisers, and Wang Qinlu, Yao Fangcheng, Wang Polu, Yang Nan, Yin Song, Pei Qi, Zhao Yao, Di Guang, Dang Shan, and the rest brigade commanders.

sentences.chinese: 時慕容沖與苻堅相攻，眾甚盛。
sentences.literal: At the time Murong Chong and Fu Jian attacked each other, and Chong's host was very large.
sentences.idiomatic: Murong Chong and Fu Jian were locked in war, and Chong's army had swollen to vast numbers.

sentences.chinese: 萇將西上，恐沖遏之，乃遣使通和，以子崇為質於沖，進屯北地，厲兵積粟，以觀時變。
sentences.literal: Chang was about to march west and feared Chong would block him, so he sent envoys to open peace and gave his son Chong as hostage to Chong; he advanced and encamped at Beidi, sharpened weapons and stored grain, to watch how the times shifted.
sentences.idiomatic: Planning a drive westward, Yao Chang feared Murong Chong might bar his path. He sued for truce, left his son Yao Chong as hostage, moved his camp to Beidi, drilled his troops and filled his granaries, and waited for the political weather to break.

sentences.chinese: 苻堅先徙晉人李祥等數千戶于敷陸，至是，降於萇，北地、新平、安定羌胡降者十餘萬戶。
sentences.literal: Fu Jian had earlier relocated several thousand households of Jin people such as Li Xiang to Fulu; at this time they surrendered to Chang, and Qiang and Hu who submitted in Beidi, Xinping, and An Ding numbered more than a hundred thousand households.
sentences.idiomatic: Fu Jian had once resettled several thousand Jin households led by Li Xiang at Fulu; they now came over to Yao Chang, and more than a hundred thousand Qiang and Hu households in Beidi, Xinping, and Anding followed suit.

sentences.chinese: 堅率諸將攻之，不能克。
sentences.literal: Jian led his generals to attack him but could not overcome him.
sentences.idiomatic: Fu Jian threw his generals against him but could not break his lines.

sentences.chinese: 萇聞容慕沖攻長安，議進趨之計，群下咸曰：「宜先據咸陽以制天下。
sentences.literal: When Chang heard that Rong Muchong was attacking Chang'an, he deliberated plans for advancing thither; his subordinates all said: "We ought first to seize Xianyang to control the realm.
sentences.idiomatic: Learning that Murong Chong (written 容慕沖 in the text) was storming Chang'an, Yao Chang called council. His officers urged, "Seize Xianyang first and the empire is yours to steer."

sentences.chinese: 」萇曰：「燕因懷舊之士而起兵，若功成事捷，咸有東歸之思，安能久固秦川！
sentences.literal: " Chang said: "Yan raised arms relying on men who long for the old; if they achieve merit and succeed, all will harbor thoughts of returning east—how could they long hold firm in the Qin riverlands!
sentences.idiomatic: Yao Chang objected. "Yan feeds on nostalgia. Once they win, every soldier will dream of home in the east. They cannot hold the Guanzhong basin for long."

sentences.chinese: 吾欲移兵嶺北，廣收資實，須秦弊燕回，然後垂拱取之。
sentences.literal: I wish to shift troops north of the ridges, broadly gather resources and supplies, wait until Qin is exhausted and Yan withdraws, then take it hands-folded.
sentences.idiomatic: I will shift my host beyond the northern ranges, gather strength and stores, and let Former Qin bleed while Yan marches away—then I can take Guanzhong without striking a blow.

sentences.chinese: 兵不血刃，坐定天下，此卞莊得二之義也。
sentences.literal: Weapons not bloodied, sit and settle the realm—this is the meaning of Bian Zhuang gaining two.
sentences.idiomatic: To settle the empire from a chair, blades unstained—that is Bian Zhuang's trick of letting two tigers tear each other.

sentences.chinese: 」堅甯朔將軍宋方率騎三千從雲中將赴長安，萇自貳縣要破之，方單馬奔免，其司馬田晃率眾降萇。
sentences.literal: " Fu Jian's General Who Calms the North Song Fang led three thousand horse from Yunzhong intending to hurry to Chang'an; Chang intercepted and destroyed him at Er County; Fang alone on horseback fled and escaped, and his major Tian Huang led the host to surrender to Chang.
sentences.idiomatic: Fu Jian's General Who Calms the North, Song Fang, was racing from Yunzhong toward Chang'an with three thousand riders when Yao Chang ambushed him at Er County. Song Fang escaped alone; his major Tian Huang surrendered the column.

sentences.chinese: 萇遣諸將攻新平，克之，因略地至安定，嶺北諸城盡降之。
sentences.literal: Chang sent generals to attack Xinping, took it, then raided territory to An Ding; all cities north of the ridges submitted to him.
sentences.idiomatic: Yao Chang's generals stormed Xinping, swept on to Anding, and every fortress north of the ranges opened its gates.

sentences.chinese: 時苻堅為慕容沖所逼，走入五將山。
sentences.literal: At the time Fu Jian was pressed by Murong Chong and fled into Mount Wujiang.
sentences.idiomatic: Fu Jian, harried by Murong Chong, fled into the Wujiang hills.

sentences.chinese: 沖入長安。
sentences.literal: Chong entered Chang'an.
sentences.idiomatic: Murong Chong took Chang'an.

sentences.chinese: 堅司隸校尉權翼、尚書趙遷、大鴻臚皇甫覆、光祿大夫薛贊、扶風太守段鏗等文武數百人奔於萇。
sentences.literal: Jian's Metropolitan Governor Quan Yi, Minister Zhao Qian, Grand Herald Huangfu Fu, Imperial Household Grandee Xue Zan, Fufeng Administrator Duan Keng, and several hundred civil and military fled to Chang.
sentences.idiomatic: Several hundred of Fu Jian's officials—among them Metropolitan Governor Quan Yi, Minister Zhao Qian, Grand Herald Huangfu Fu, Palace Grandee Xue Zan, and Fufeng prefect Duan Keng—rode to Yao Chang's camp.

sentences.chinese: 萇遣驍騎將軍吳忠率騎圍堅，萇如新平。
sentences.literal: Chang sent Fierce Cavalry General Wu Zhong to lead horse to surround Jian; Chang himself went to Xinping.
sentences.idiomatic: Yao Chang sent Fierce Cavalry General Wu Zhong to ring Fu Jian with cavalry while he himself rode to Xinping.

sentences.chinese: 俄而忠執堅，送之。
sentences.literal: Soon Zhong seized Jian and delivered him.
sentences.idiomatic: Wu Zhong soon seized Fu Jian and brought him in.

sentences.chinese: 慕容沖遣其車騎大將軍高蓋率眾五萬來伐，戰于新平南，大破之，蓋率麾下數千人來降，拜散騎常侍。
sentences.literal: Murong Chong sent his Cavalry and Chariots Grand General Gao Gai to lead fifty thousand to attack; they fought south of Xinping, and he was greatly defeated; Gai led several thousand under his command to come surrender, and was appointed Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary.
sentences.idiomatic: Murong Chong ordered Gao Gai, his Cavalry and Chariots commander, against Yao Chang with fifty thousand men. South of Xinping Yao Chang shattered the army; Gao Gai brought a few thousand survivors over and was named Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary.

sentences.chinese: 沖既率眾東下，長安空虛。
sentences.literal: After Chong led his host eastward, Chang'an was empty.
sentences.idiomatic: Once Murong Chong marched east, Chang'an stood hollowed out.

sentences.chinese: 盧水郝奴稱帝于長安，渭北盡應之。
sentences.literal: Lushui Hao Nu declared himself emperor in Chang'an, and all north of the Wei responded to him.
sentences.idiomatic: Hao Nu of the Lushui tribes proclaimed himself emperor in Chang'an, and the north bank of the Wei rose at his call.

sentences.chinese: 扶風王驎有眾數千，保據馬嵬。
sentences.literal: Wang Lin of Fufeng had several thousand men and held Macang.
sentences.idiomatic: Wang Lin of Fufeng held Macang with a few thousand followers.

sentences.chinese: 奴遣弟多攻驎。
sentences.literal: Nu sent younger brother Duo to attack Lin.
sentences.idiomatic: Hao Nu sent his brother Duo against him.

sentences.chinese: 萇伐驎，破之，驎走漢中。
sentences.literal: Chang campaigned against Lin, defeated him, and Lin fled to Hanzhong.
sentences.idiomatic: Yao Chang struck Wang Lin, broke his line, and drove him into Hanzhong.

sentences.chinese: 執多而進攻奴，降之。
sentences.literal: He seized Duo then advanced to attack Nu and made him surrender.
sentences.idiomatic: He captured Duo, then wheeled on Hao Nu and forced his submission.

sentences.chinese: 乙太元十一年萇僭即皇帝位於長安，大赦，改元曰建初，國號大秦，改長安曰常安。
sentences.literal: In the eleventh year of Jin's Taiyuan era Chang usurpingly assumed the emperor's position at Chang'an, proclaimed a general amnesty, changed the era to Jianchu, took the state name Great Qin, and changed the name of the capital from Chang'an to Changan (常安, "Constant Peace").
sentences.idiomatic: In the eleventh year of the Taiyuan era Yao Chang seized the throne at Chang'an, ordered a general amnesty, adopted the reign name Jianchu, styled his state Great Qin, and renamed the capital Chang'an to Changan ("Constant Peace").

sentences.chinese: 立妻虵氏為皇后，子興為皇太子，置百官。
sentences.literal: He established wife She as empress, son Xing as heir apparent, and set up the hundred offices.
sentences.idiomatic: He raised his consort of the She clan to empress, invested his son Yao Xing as crown prince, and filled out the imperial bureaucracy.

sentences.chinese: 自謂以火德承苻氏木行，服色如漢氏承周故事。
sentences.literal: He claimed that by fire virtue he succeeded the Fu clan's wood phase, and dress colors followed Han's succeeding Zhou precedent.
sentences.idiomatic: He claimed the Mandate of Fire to follow Fu's Wood, and chose court colors by the Han precedent that had succeeded Zhou.

sentences.chinese: 徙安定五千餘戶于長安。
sentences.literal: He relocated more than five thousand households from An Ding to Chang'an.
sentences.idiomatic: He moved over five thousand Anding households into the capital.

sentences.chinese: 以弟征虜緒為司隸校尉，鎮長安。
sentences.literal: He made younger brother Conquering the Enemy Xu Metropolitan Governor and garrisoned Chang'an.
sentences.idiomatic: He gave his brother Yao Xu, General Who Conquers the Enemy, the metropolitan post and left him to hold Changan.

sentences.chinese: 萇如安定，擊平涼胡金熙、鮮卑沒奕於，大破之。
sentences.literal: Chang went to An Ding, attacked Pingliang Hu Jin Xi and Xianbei Moboyi Yu, and greatly defeated them.
sentences.idiomatic: Yao Chang marched to Anding, smashed the Pingliang Di leader Jin Xi and the Xianbei chief Moboyi Yu, and scattered their hosts.

sentences.chinese: 遂如秦州，與苻堅秦州刺史王統相持，天水屠各、略陽羌胡應萇者二萬餘戶，統懼，乃降。
sentences.literal: Then he went to Qinzhou and stood off against Fu Jian's Qinzhou Inspector Wang Tong; Tuge of Tianshui and Qiang and Hu of Lüeyang who responded to Chang numbered more than twenty thousand households; Tong feared and then surrendered.
sentences.idiomatic: He pressed into Qinzhou against Fu Jian's inspector Wang Tong until Tianshui Tuge and Lüeyang Qiang and Hu—more than twenty thousand households—rallied to Yao Chang. Wang Tong, terrified, capitulated.

sentences.chinese: 因饗將士於上邽，南安人古成詵進曰：「臣州人殷地險，俊傑如林，用武之國也。
sentences.literal: Thereupon he feasted officers and soldiers at Shanggui; Gucheng Shen of Nan'an advanced and said: "My prefecture's people are abundant and the land rugged; outstanding men are like a forest—it is a state for wielding arms.
sentences.idiomatic: At a victory banquet in Shanggui, Gucheng Shen of Nan'an spoke up: "My home commandery is populous, its terrain cruel, its heroes thick as trees—a land born for war."

sentences.chinese: 王秦州不能收拔賢才，三分鼎足，而坐玩珠玉，以至於此。
sentences.literal: Prince Qinzhou could not gather and elevate worthy talent or form a tripartite tripod stance, but sat fondling pearls and jade, until it came to this.
sentences.idiomatic: Yet Inspector Wang never gathered men fit to divide the realm three ways; he sat fondling gems until ruin found him.

sentences.chinese: 陛下宜散秦州金帛以施六軍，旌賢表善以副鄙州之望。
sentences.literal: Your Majesty ought to distribute Qinzhou's gold and silk to supply the six armies, honor the worthy and display the good, to match my humble prefecture's hopes.
sentences.idiomatic: Scatter Qinzhou's gold and silk among the hosts, honor the able and the loyal, and you will answer what my people pray for.

sentences.chinese: 」萇善之，擢為尚書郎。
sentences.literal: " Chang approved and promoted him to Gentleman of the Secretariat.
sentences.idiomatic: Yao Chang agreed and raised him to a secretariat post.

sentences.chinese: 拜弟碩德都督隴右諸軍事、征西將軍、秦州刺史，領護東羌校尉，鎮上邽。
sentences.literal: He appointed younger brother Shuo de Area Commander-in-Chief of Longyou, General Who Conquers the West, Qinzhou Inspector, concurrently Colonel Who Protects the Eastern Qiang, and garrisoned Shanggui.
sentences.idiomatic: He named his brother Yao Shuode commander of Longyou, General Who Conquers the West, Qinzhou inspector, and Colonel of the Eastern Qiang, with headquarters at Shanggui.

sentences.chinese: 萇還安定，修德政，布惠化，省非急之費，以救時弊，閭閻之士有豪介之善者，皆顯異之。
sentences.literal: Chang returned to An Ding, cultivated virtuous government, spread beneficent transformation, cut non-urgent expenses to remedy the times' ills, and for gentlemen of the lanes who had heroic integrity's goodness he all distinguished them exceptionally.
sentences.idiomatic: Back in Anding he pursued humane rule, spread relief, slashed needless spending, and singled out commoners of stubborn integrity for honor.

sentences.chinese: 萇復如秦州，為苻登所敗，語在《登傳》。
sentences.literal: Chang again went to Qinzhou, was defeated by Fu Deng—the account is in Deng's biography.
sentences.idiomatic: Yao Chang returned to Qinzhou and lost to Fu Deng, as told in Deng's memoir.

sentences.chinese: 以其太子興鎮長安，而與登相距。
sentences.literal: He posted his heir Xing to garrison Chang'an while he opposed Deng at a distance.
sentences.idiomatic: He left crown prince Yao Xing to hold Changan while he faced Fu Deng in the field.

sentences.chinese: 登馮翊太守蘭犢與苻師奴離貳，慕容永攻之，犢遣使請救。
sentences.literal: Deng's Fengyi Administrator Lan Du and Fu Shinu were at odds; Murong Yong attacked him; Du sent envoys asking rescue.
sentences.idiomatic: Fu Deng's Fengyi prefect Lan Du had broken with Fu Shinu; Murong Yong fell upon Lan Du, who begged Yao Chang for aid.

sentences.chinese: 萇將赴救，尚書令姚旻、左僕射尹緯等言於萇曰：「苻登近在瓦亭，陛下未宜輕舉。
sentences.literal: Chang was about to go to the rescue; Director of the Secretariat Yao Min, Left Vice Director Yin Wei, and others said to Chang: "Fu Deng is near at Wating; Your Majesty ought not move lightly.
sentences.idiomatic: As Yao Chang prepared to march, Yao Min and Yin Wei warned him, "Fu Deng sits close at Wating; this is no moment for a rash advance."

sentences.chinese: 」萇曰：「登遲重少決，每失時機，聞吾自行，正當廣集兵資，必不能輕軍深入。
sentences.literal: " Chang said: "Deng is sluggish and heavy, seldom decisive, always misses the moment for action; hearing I march myself, he will only broadly gather troops and supplies—he certainly cannot with a light army push deep.
sentences.idiomatic: Yao Chang answered, "Fu Deng is slow and hesitant; he always misses his moment. If he hears I have taken the field he will hoard supplies and dare not strike deep with a light column."

sentences.chinese: 兩月之間，足可克此三豎，吾事必矣。
sentences.literal: Within two months it is enough to overcome these three wretches—my affair is settled.
sentences.idiomatic: Two months will suffice to break those three upstarts; then the way is clear for me.

sentences.chinese: 」遂師次於渥源。
sentences.literal: " Thereupon the army halted at Woyuan.
sentences.idiomatic: He encamped the army at Woyuan.

sentences.chinese: 師奴率眾來距，大戰，敗之，盡俘其眾。
sentences.literal: Shinu led the host to oppose; they fought a great battle, defeated him, and took all his host captive.
sentences.idiomatic: Fu Shinu marched to meet him; Yao Chang shattered his line and took every survivor.

sentences.chinese: 又擒蘭犢，收其士馬。
sentences.literal: He also seized Lan Du and collected his soldiers and horses.
sentences.idiomatic: He seized Lan Du as well and absorbed his cavalry.

sentences.chinese: 萇乃掘苻堅屍，鞭撻無數，裸剝衣裳，薦之以棘，坎土而埋之。
sentences.literal: Chang then dug up Fu Jian's corpse, whipped it countless times, stripped the clothing naked, laid it on thorns, and buried it in earthen pit.
sentences.idiomatic: Yao Chang had Fu Jian's corpse dug up, flogged it beyond counting, stripped it bare, rolled it on brambles, and heaped earth over the ruin.

sentences.chinese: 慕容永征西將軍王宣率眾降萇。
sentences.literal: Murong Yong's General Who Conquers the West Wang Xuan led the host to surrender to Chang.
sentences.idiomatic: Wang Xuan, Murong Yong's western commander, brought his army over to Yao Chang.

sentences.chinese: 初，關西雄傑以苻氏既終，萇雄略命世，天下之事可一旦而定。
sentences.literal: At first, heroes west of the Pass thought the Fu clan was already ended, Chang's heroic strategy commanded the age, and the realm's affairs could be settled in a morning.
sentences.idiomatic: Once, every champion beyond the Pass believed Fu was finished and Yao Chang's genius owned the hour—that the empire could be settled in a single dawn.

sentences.chinese: 萇既與苻登相持積年，數為登所敗，遠近咸懷去就之計，唯征虜齊難、冠軍徐洛生、輔國劉郭單、冠威彌姐婆觸、龍驤趙惡地、鎮北梁國兒等守忠不貳，並留子弟守營，供繼軍糧，身將精卒，隨萇征伐。
sentences.literal: After Chang had faced Fu Deng for accumulated years, repeatedly was defeated by Deng, far and near all harbored plans of staying or leaving; only Conquering the Enemy Qi Nan, Champion Xu Luosheng, Support of the State Liu Guodan, Crown Might Mijie Potu, Dragon-Soaring Zhao Wudi, Garrison the North Liang Guo'er, and others kept loyalty undivided; together they left sons and younger brothers to guard camp, supplied successive army grain, personally led picked troops, and followed Chang on campaigns.
sentences.idiomatic: Years of stalemate with Fu Deng, and repeated defeat, made allies far and near weigh betrayal—yet Qi Nan, Xu Luosheng, Liu Guodan, Mijie Potu, Zhao Wudi, Liang Guo'er, and a handful of others never wavered, left sons to guard their camps, fed Yao Chang's army, and rode with him in person.

sentences.chinese: 時諸營既多，故號萇軍為大營，大營之號自此始也。
sentences.literal: At the time the various camps were already many, therefore Chang's army was styled the Great Camp—the title Great Camp began from this.
sentences.idiomatic: So many satellite camps sprang up that men called Yao Chang's host the Great Camp—a name born in those days.

sentences.chinese: 時天大雪，萇下書深自責罰，散後宮文綺珍寶以供戎事，身食一味，妻不重彩。
sentences.literal: At the time heaven snowed heavily; Chang issued a document deeply blaming and punishing himself, scattered rear-palace patterned silks and treasures to supply military affairs, himself ate one flavor, wives wore no heavy colors.
sentences.idiomatic: When blizzards struck he published a self-rebuke, auctioned the harem's silks and jewels for the war chest, ate a single plain dish, and forbade his consorts rich dress.

sentences.chinese: 將帥死王事者，加秩二等，士卒戰沒，皆有褒贈。
sentences.literal: For generals who died in royal service, ranks were raised two grades; for soldiers fallen in battle, all had posthumous honors and gifts.
sentences.idiomatic: Generals who died in service gained two extra ranks of pension; every common soldier killed in action received a stipend for his kin.

sentences.chinese: 立太學，禮先賢之後。
sentences.literal: He established the Imperial Academy and honored the descendants of former worthies.
sentences.idiomatic: He founded an imperial academy and endowed the heirs of ancient sages.

sentences.chinese: 敦煌索盧曜請刺苻登，萇曰：「卿以身徇難，將為誰乎？
sentences.literal: Dunhuang Suolu Yao asked to assassinate Fu Deng; Chang said: "You use your body to die for hardship—for whom will it be?
sentences.idiomatic: Suolu Yao of Dunhuang volunteered to murder Fu Deng. Yao Chang asked, "You mean to throw your life away—but for whose gain?"

sentences.chinese: 」曜曰：「臣死之後，深以友人隴西辛暹仰托。
sentences.literal: " Yao said: "After your servant dies, I deeply entrust to you my friend Longxi Xin Xian, looking up.
sentences.idiomatic: Suolu Yao replied, "When I am gone, let my friend Xin Xian of Longxi take my place in your service."

sentences.chinese: 」萇遣之。
sentences.literal: " Chang sent him.
sentences.idiomatic: Yao Chang let him go.

sentences.chinese: 事發，為登所殺，萇以暹為騎都尉。
sentences.literal: When the affair broke, Deng killed him; Chang appointed Xian Cavalry Commandant.
sentences.idiomatic: The plot surfaced; Fu Deng executed him, and Yao Chang named Xin Xian a cavalry commandant.

sentences.chinese: 登進逼安定，諸將勸萇決戰，萇曰：「與窮寇競勝，兵家之下。
sentences.literal: Deng advanced pressing An Ding; generals urged Chang to fight a decisive battle; Chang said: "With a cornered foe competing for victory is the lowest of the military art.
sentences.idiomatic: As Fu Deng closed on Anding his generals demanded a pitched battle. Yao Chang refused. "To wrestle a desperate enemy for glory is the meanest stratagem in the canon."

sentences.chinese: 吾將以計取之。
sentences.literal: I will take him by stratagem.
sentences.idiomatic: I mean to break him by craft.

sentences.chinese: 」於是留其尚書令姚旻守安定，夜襲登輜重於大界，克之。
sentences.literal: " Thereupon he left his Director of the Secretariat Yao Min to guard An Ding, night-raided Deng's baggage train at Dajie, and took it.
sentences.idiomatic: He left Yao Min to hold Anding, slipped by night against Fu Deng's baggage column at Dajie, and overran it.

sentences.chinese: 諸將或欲因登駭亂擊之，萇曰：「登眾雖亂，怒氣猶盛，未可輕也。
sentences.literal: Some generals wished to strike Deng while he was panic-stricken and in disorder; Chang said: "Though Deng's host is in disorder, angry qi is still strong—he cannot be treated lightly.
sentences.idiomatic: Some urged a follow-up blow while Fu Deng reeled. Yao Chang said no: "His ranks may waver, but their rage still runs high—do not despise them."

sentences.chinese: 」遂止。
sentences.literal: " Thereupon he stopped.
sentences.idiomatic: He held his hand.

sentences.chinese: 萇以安定地狹，且逼苻登，使姚碩德鎮安定，徙安定千餘家安于陰密，遣弟征南靖鎮之。
sentences.literal: Because An Ding's territory was narrow and Deng pressed close, Chang had Yao Shuo de garrison An Ding, relocated more than a thousand households from An Ding and settled them at Yinmi, and sent younger brother Conquering the South Jing to garrison it.
sentences.idiomatic: Anding was cramped under Fu Deng's shadow, so Yao Chang stationed Yao Shuode there, moved a thousand Anding families into Yinmi, and sent his brother Yao Jing, General Who Conquers the South, to hold the new line.

sentences.chinese: 立社稷于長安。
sentences.literal: He established the altars of soil and grain at Chang'an.
sentences.idiomatic: He dedicated the state altars at Changan.

sentences.chinese: 百姓年七十有德行者，拜為中大夫，歲賜牛酒。
sentences.literal: For commoners aged seventy who had virtuous conduct, he appointed them Central Grand Masters and yearly gifted oxen and wine.
sentences.idiomatic: Commoners past seventy known for virtue were named grand counselors of the palace and given oxen and wine each year.

sentences.chinese: 尹緯、姚晃謂古成詵曰：「苻登窮寇，歷年未滅，奸雄鴟峙，所在糾扇，夷夏皆貳，將若之何？
sentences.literal: Yin Wei and Yao Huang said to Gucheng Shen: "Fu Deng is a cornered foe, years without being destroyed; traitors stand like hawks, everywhere gather and fan; barbarian and Chinese both are double-minded—what shall be done?
sentences.idiomatic: Yin Wei and Yao Huang asked Gucheng Shen, "Fu Deng still survives after all these years; every strongman preens like a hawk and fans revolt; tribesmen and Chinese alike waver—what now?"

sentences.chinese: 」詵曰：「主上權略無方，信賞必罰，賢能之士，咸懷樂推，豈慮大業不成，氐賊不滅乎！
sentences.literal: " Shen said: "Our lord's stratagem has no bound, trust rewards and sure punishments; men of worth and ability all harbor willing praise—why worry great enterprise will not succeed or Di rebels will not be destroyed!
sentences.idiomatic: Gucheng Shen answered, "Our lord's designs know no limit; he rewards faith and punishes without mercy; every able man gladly lifts him up. Why doubt the great work—or that the Di bandit will fall?"

sentences.chinese: 」緯曰：「登窮寇未滅，奸雄所在扇合，吾等寧無懼乎？
sentences.literal: " Wei said: "Deng cornered foe not destroyed, traitors everywhere fan and unite—should we have no fear?
sentences.idiomatic: Yin Wei pressed him: "While Fu Deng lives and rogues flock everywhere, should we not be afraid?"

sentences.chinese: 」詵曰：「三秦天府之國，主上十分已有其八。
sentences.literal: " Shen said: "The three Qin are Heaven's treasury-land; our lord already has eight of ten parts.
sentences.idiomatic: Gucheng Shen said, "The three Qin are heaven's own granary; our lord already holds eight parts in ten."

sentences.chinese: 今所在可慮者，苻登、楊定、雷惡地耳，自餘瑣瑣，焉足論哉！
sentences.literal: Those to worry about now are only Fu Deng, Yang Ding, and Lei Wudi; the rest petty—how worth discussing!
sentences.idiomatic: Only Fu Deng, Yang Ding, and Lei Wudi still matter; the rest are gnats unworthy of talk.

sentences.chinese: 然惡地地狹眾寡，不足為憂。
sentences.literal: Yet Lei Wudi's territory is narrow and his host is few—not enough to be a worry.
sentences.idiomatic: Lei Wudi holds thin ground and few spears—hardly worth a second thought.
